title: Choose the Maximum Number of Investment Opportunities
real_world_story: A financial planning system has a limited number of available investment slots. Each investment requires a certain amount of capital, and the planner wants to select as many opportunities as possible without exceeding the available budget.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Capital requirements of available investment opportunities
real_world_connection.target_represents: Maximum number of investment opportunities that can be selected
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Selecting the least expensive available opportunities first to maximize the number of selected investments

problem_statement: Given N investment opportunities and a total investment budget B, determine the maximum number of opportunities that can be selected without exceeding the budget. Each opportunity can be selected at most once.
task: Select as many investment opportunities as possible while keeping the total investment cost within the available budget.
input_format: The first line contains two integers N and B, representing the number of investment opportunities and the available budget. The second line contains N space-separated integers representing the cost of each investment opportunity.
output_format: Print the maximum number of investment opportunities that can be selected within the budget.

examples.explanation: Selecting investments costing 2, 3, and 5 uses 10 units of the budget. Four investments would require at least 2+3+5+7=17, which exceeds the budget.
The two least expensive investments cost 3 and 4, so two opportunities can be selected within the budget.

expected_algorithm.name: Greedy
expected_algorithm.reason: Choosing the least expensive investment opportunities first maximizes the number of opportunities that can fit within the fixed budget.

complexity.additional_note: The sorting operation dominates the running time.

hint: Sort the investment costs in ascending order.
Start selecting from the least expensive opportunity.
Keep adding costs while the total remains within the budget.
The number of selected opportunities is the answer.
real_world_takeaway: A greedy strategy can quickly maximize the number of affordable investment opportunities when every selected opportunity has the same selection value and only its cost matters.
